title: sub_gallery_panel.dart (601 lines) is built by no screen -- only by a widget test -- while the code claims the narrative view uses it
what_happened: Grepping every .dart file under packages/ and apps/ finds exactly one construction of SubGalleryPanel, in packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/session_review/sub_cull_rail_dynamic_subs_test.dart:102. Neither narrative_view.dart nor workbench_view.dart references it, and driving the app confirms it: the narrative view renders hero preview, Night Doctor, improvement curve, findings, project growth and the calibration cards, and contains no sub grid at all. sub_cull_rail.dart:24 states 'One controller, two renderings: the narrative screen uses SubGalleryPanel', which is not true of the shipped build.
expected: Either the narrative view shows the sub gallery (as the comment says and as the two-renderings design implies), or the dead panel and its comment are deleted. As shipped, a user reviewing a night in Narrative mode has no way to see, blink, accept or reject individual subs without switching to Workbench.
repro: 1. Open Session Review for any session. 2. Stay in Narrative and scroll top to bottom -- no sub grid appears. 3. grep -rn 'SubGalleryPanel(' packages apps --include='*.dart' -> one hit, in a test.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-07.png, rsr-09.png, rsr-10.png cover the entire narrative scroll: sections are 'How deep is deep enough?', 'What I fixed and found', 'This project over time', 'Calibrated & annotated'. grep output as above.
proposed_fix: Mount SubGalleryPanel in narrative_view.dart under a 'Your subs' section, or delete the file and correct the sub_cull_rail doc comment.
verdict_reasoning: grep -rn 'SubGalleryPanel' over packages/ and apps/ returns the class definition, three comment mentions in sub_cull_rail.dart, and exactly one construction: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/session_review/sub_cull_rail_dynamic_subs_test.dart:102. narrative_view.dart builds NightReportPanel (verdict + findings), ImprovementCurvePanel and GrowthCurvePanel and nothing else -- no sub grid. The false claim is verbatim at sub_cull_rail.dart:24: 'One controller, two renderings: the narrative screen uses [SubGalleryPanel]'. Location correct; P3 is right (601 dead lines plus a comment that lies about the shipped composition).

title: Stack & Share surfaces the raw Rust error enum to the user: 'SkotiqError.imageError(field0: ...)'
what_happened: Both failures rendered in the dialog's error card verbatim as 'SkotiqError.imageError(field0: Failed to initialize stacker: Reference frame has only 0 stars, need at least 5 for alignment)' and 'SkotiqError.imageError(field0: Alignment residual too high: 10.34px (max 10.00px))'. The wrapper type name and the flutter_rust_bridge positional-field label 'field0:' are shown to the operator.
expected: Show the message only, plus an actionable next step ('No stars were detected in the reference frame. Check focus, or turn off Apply calibration.'), with the raw type available behind a 'technical details' disclosure like ErrorDialog already provides elsewhere in this app.
repro: 1. Imaging > Stack > Stack & Share > Start on any 16-bit FITS session. 2. Read the red card.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/stack_result/stack_and_share_dialog.dart error rendering; the message is the toString() of the bridge SkotiqError.
location_wrong: The raw stringification is packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/stack_and_share_provider.dart:234 (`errorMessage: e.toString()`); stack_and_share_dialog.dart:258-282 only renders it.
proposed_fix: Unwrap SkotiqError to its payload string when rendering, and keep the full toString() in a collapsible technical-details section.
verdict_reasoning: Followed the string end to end. packages/skotiq_bridge/lib/src/error.dart:85 is `const factory SkotiqError.imageError(String field0)` and the generated toString is verbatim `return 'SkotiqError.imageError(field0: $field0)';` at error.freezed.dart:1557 -- the flutter_rust_bridge positional label really is in the string. stack_and_share_provider.dart:234 stores `errorMessage: e.toString()` unmodified; stack_and_share_dialog.dart:243-245 hands it to _buildError, which at :258-282 special-cases only the live-stacking-busy case and otherwise renders the raw string as the message of a 'Stack & Share failed' alert. No mapping table, no technical-details disclosure, and the only pre-formatted message is the remote-backend refusal at :171-176. Severity: presentation polish on an already-legible sentence, so P3 rather than P2.

title: Science CSV exports never ask where to save and write to a hard-coded ~/Documents/Skotiq/exports, ignoring the app's configured data directory
what_happened: Pressing CSV on 'Photometry Measurements' produced no save dialog at all; the toast read 'Exported 495 rows to /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/photometry_2026-08-02T11-16-14.csv'. This instance was launched with SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR and SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR pointed at /tmp/ns-audit/r-science-review/data, and the export ignored both. Every other export I drove in this sweep (stack PNG/JPEG, Share Card, AstroBin) opens a GTK save dialog and honours the chosen path, so the science hub is the odd one out. The shared hard-coded directory is also a collision point: it already contained an mpc_report written at the same minute by a different concurrently-running instance.
expected: Either open the same save dialog the other exports use, or write into the app's configured data directory and say so. A user who has moved their Skotiq data to another disk will not find these files, and a headless/appliance install may not have a Documents directory at all.
repro: 1. Launch with SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR set somewhere other than the default. 2. Analytics > Science > toolbar database icon > any 'CSV' button. 3. No file picker appears; read the toast path.
evidence: AT-SPI: 'Exported 495 rows to /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/photometry_2026-08-02T11-16-14.csv'. `ls /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/` shows the file plus artefacts from other audit profiles. The sandbox dir /tmp/ns-audit/r-science-review/ received nothing.
proposed_fix: Route the CSV writes through the same file-picker helper the stack exports use, defaulting the suggested directory to the configured data dir.
verdict_reasoning: science_export_hub.dart:41-48 defines scienceExportDirectoryProvider as getApplicationDocumentsDirectory() + 'Skotiq/exports', created on demand; _exportData at :726-855 builds the CSV, reads that provider at :826, joins a timestamped filename and writes it with no picker anywhere in the path -- the only user-facing surface is the 'Exported N rows to <path>' string at :831. getApplicationDocumentsDirectory is path_provider's XDG documents dir, which nothing in the SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR / SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR plumbing overrides, so the export does ignore the configured data directory. The contrast the finding draws is real too: stack-result exports go through stackResultSavePickerProvider with a dialogTitle/fileName (stack_result_screen.dart:869-874). Location correct. Severity: P3 rather than P2 -- the file is written, the full path is reported in the result line, and on mobile revealExportedFile (:846) hands it to the share sheet; the harm is an unexpected location and a shared collision point, not lost data.

title: The stack result's 'Avg HFR' statistic never renders because the service hard-codes avgHfr: null, even though every selected sub carries an HFR
what_happened: stack_result_screen.dart:522 renders an 'Avg HFR ... px' row only `if (result.avgHfr != null)`, and stack_and_share_service.dart:425 persists `avgHfr: null` unconditionally. So the row is dead: two real Stack & Share runs in this session wrote stacked_results rows 2 and 3 with avg_hfr NULL, while every one of their source frames has hfr = 2.4 in captured_images. The only row in the table with an avg_hfr is one I seeded by hand. The result panel therefore shows Integration / Frames stacked / Rejected / Avg residual / Filter / Dimensions and silently omits the one number an imager actually judges a stack by.
expected: Average the HFR of the frames that were integrated (they are already in hand as StackedFrameSelection rows) and persist it, so the panel shows 'Avg HFR 2.40 px'.
repro: 1. Run Stack & Share to completion. 2. The result panel has no Avg HFR row. 3. sqlite3 skotiq.db 'select id,frames_stacked,avg_hfr from stacked_results' -> 2|7|(null), 3|8|(null); 'select distinct hfr from captured_images where session_id=3' -> 2.4.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-11.png (Integration panel with no HFR row). DB as above. Source: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/stack_and_share_service.dart:425 `avgHfr: null,`.
proposed_fix: Compute the mean HFR over the frames whose add succeeded and pass it in place of the null.
verdict_reasoning: Both cited lines are exact in the current tree. stack_and_share_service.dart:425 is `avgHfr: null,` (unconditional, in the single StackAndShareResult the run persists) and stack_result_screen.dart:522 is `if (result.avgHfr != null)` guarding the 'Avg HFR' _StatRow. No other local producer sets it -- the only other references are stacking_operations.dart:251 reading it back off a remote host's JSON (fed by this same null on the host) and stacked_results_dao.dart:164 reading the column. So on the local path the column is always NULL and the row can never render. The source now carries a justification comment ('the live-stacking engine does not measure HFR ... a later analysis pass may populate it'), so it is a known gap rather than an oversight, but the factual claim -- dead UI row, hard-coded null -- holds and the file:line is right. P3 correct.

title: The standalone /science route can never build ScienceScreen -- its redirect always fires, so the screen class and its Scaffold are unreachable code
what_happened: app_router.dart declares the /science GoRoute with BOTH a `redirect` that unconditionally returns '/analytics?tab=science...' and a `pageBuilder` that constructs ScienceScreen. In go_router a non-null redirect short-circuits the route, so the pageBuilder never runs. ScienceScreen is constructed in exactly one place in the whole repo -- that dead pageBuilder -- so the class, its Scaffold and its initialTabQuery plumbing ship but can never appear. Driving the app confirms it: every route into science lands on the Analytics shell with the Science tab selected, never on a standalone science screen.
expected: Delete the dead pageBuilder (and ScienceScreen with it) or drop the redirect if a standalone screen is actually wanted. Leaving both is a trap: a future reader editing ScienceScreen will change nothing that ships.
repro: 1. Reach science by every available path -- Dashboard cockpit narrator, imaging science HUD, sequencer light-curve panel, transients screen. 2. All land on Analytics with the Science tab active (header reads 'Analytics', sub-tabs Science / First Light / Observing Alerts). 3. grep -rn 'ScienceScreen' packages apps --include='*.dart' -> only the definition and app_router.dart:232.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-23.png (the only rendering of the science workspace is inside the Analytics shell). packages/skotiq_app/lib/router/app_router.dart:222-236: `redirect: (context, state) { ... return '/analytics?tab=science...'; }` followed by `pageBuilder: ... child: ScienceScreen(initialTabQuery: tabQuery)`.
proposed_fix: Remove the pageBuilder from the /science route and delete ScienceScreen, keeping ScienceWorkspaceView as the single implementation.
verdict_reasoning: app_router.dart:222-236 is exactly as described: the '/science' GoRoute declares `redirect: (context, state) { final sub = state.uri.queryParameters['tab']; return '/analytics?tab=science...'; }` -- an unconditional non-null return -- followed by a pageBuilder constructing ScienceScreen. go_router short-circuits a route whose redirect returns non-null, so the pageBuilder is unreachable. app_router.dart:232 is the only construction of ScienceScreen in packages/ or apps/ (other hits are the definition at science_screen.dart:246/249 and a doc comment at :42). Corroborated live: navigating to Science lands on the Analytics shell with sub-tabs Science / First Light / Observing Alerts (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sr-08.png), never a standalone screen. Cited locations exact; P3 is generous (cost is dead code plus the trap it sets) but not wrong.
